data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"If the token budget is reserved atomically per-event before event generation begins, then exhaustion can only prevent the next event from starting\u2014it can never interrupt an in-progress write. This makes every budget-exhaustion halt clean by construction, so resumption is always safe as long as the log's append-only identity is intact. The only refusal case is log corruption from causes other than budget exhaustion (hardware failure, concurrent writes). The cost is potential underutilization of the global budget pool and the need to estimate per-event token costs before generation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The per-event budget estimate is inaccurate and the actual token cost exceeds the reservation, causing mid-write exhaustion despite the guard.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The budget accountant and the event writer are not atomically coordinated\u2014budget is reserved but the write is not yet started, and exhaustion is raised in the gap.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Underutilization is severe enough that the system frequently halts with substantial unused budget, making the approach impractical.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log is corrupted by non-budget causes (crash, storage failure) even though the halt itself was clean.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The reservation mechanism itself consumes tokens (metadata writes), creating a recursive budget problem.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Before generating event N+1, the system checks whether the remaining budget can cover the maximum possible event size. If not, it halts cleanly\u2014event N is the committed tail, and no partial N+1 exists. If yes, it reserves the budget and proceeds. The reservation is released on commit (actual tokens used may be less than reserved). This collapses the 'clean halt' condition into normal operation: there is no code path where exhaustion interrupts a write. Resumption appends after N, which is always a complete event.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
